subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 30-year-old woman and her 32-year-old husband are healthy and have a 2-year-old son with developmental regression, an exaggerated startle response, and a cherry-red spot; enzyme studies show absent hexosaminidase A. Genetic testing shows that both parents carry a pathogenic variant.
question: What is the probability that their next child will be affected by this disease?
explanation_correct: Tay-Sachs disease is autosomal recessive, so an affected child inherits one pathogenic variant from each carrier parent. Each pregnancy therefore carries a 25% chance of an affected child, a 50% chance of a healthy carrier, and a 25% chance of a healthy noncarrier.

explanation_incorrect.A: A 0% risk would apply only if both parents were homozygous for normal alleles, which is not the case here.
explanation_incorrect.B: A 50% figure is the probability that a child will be an asymptomatic carrier, not affected.
explanation_incorrect.C: A 75% figure is the probability that a child will not be affected, not the probability of being affected.
explanation_incorrect.E: A 100% risk would require every child to inherit a pathogenic variant from each parent, which does not occur in autosomal recessive disease.

educationalObjective: Tay-Sachs disease is autosomal recessive, so two carrier parents have a 25% risk of an affected child in each pregnancy.
